# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.

Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. # Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. # Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

# Guideline
Subject: Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR)
## Chapter 1 – Overview of risk-based capital requirements
Effective Date: November 2023 / January 2024
Note: For institutions with a fiscal year ending October 31 or December 31, respectively.
Subsections 485(1) and 949(1) of the Bank Act (BA), subsection 473(1) of the Trust and Loan Companies Act (TLCA) require banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies to maintain adequate capital. The CAR Guideline is not made pursuant to subsections 485(2) or 949(2) of the BA, or to subsection 473(2) of the TLCA. However, the capital standards set out in this guideline together with the leverage requirements set out in the Leverage Requirements Guideline provide the framework within which the Superintendent assesses whether a bank, a bank holding company, a trust company, or a loan company maintains adequate capital pursuant to the Acts. For this purpose, the Superintendent has established two minimum standards: the leverage ratio described in the Leverage Requirements Guideline, and the risk-based capital ratio described in this guideline. The first test provides an overall measure of the adequacy of an institution's capital, while the second measure focuses on risk faced by the institution. Notwithstanding that a bank, bank holding company, trust company, or loan company may meet these standards, the Superintendent may direct a bank or bank holding company to increase its capital under subsections 485(3) or 949(3) of the BA, or a trust company or a loan company to increase its capital under subsection 473(3) of the TLCA.
OSFI, as a member of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, participated in the development of the Basel capital framework on which this guideline is based. Where relevant, the Basel framework paragraph numbers are provided in square brackets at the end of each paragraph referencing material from the Basel framework.
The capital and leverage requirements for domestic systemically important banks are supplemented by the requirements described in OSFI's Total Loss Absorbing Capacity (TLAC) Guideline.

phase2_data.synthesis:
## Overall Assessment

The document demonstrates **good compliance** with the template, providing a comprehensive overview of the risk-based capital requirements for banks, bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies in Canada. The content covers the key conceptual domains, including the purpose, scope, mandatory requirements, operational expectations, and references to supporting documents.

## Critical Gaps

- **Lack of Defined Roles and Responsibilities** (throughout): The document does not explicitly assign role-level accountability for compliance with the capital adequacy requirements, which could lead to gaps in implementation and monitoring.
- **Insufficient Details on Oversight and Escalation Processes** (pages 2-5): The document does not provide clear details on the specific oversight processes, challenge mechanisms, or escalation procedures that the Superintendent would use to assess capital adequacy.
- **Absence of Review Cadence and Assurance Expectations** (pages 7-9): The document lacks information on the frequency of review, reporting requirements, or independent assurance processes that institutions must follow to ensure ongoing compliance.

## Improvement Areas

### Clarity (pages 2, 4, 6)
- Some instances where the tone is more advisory or suggestive rather than directive, which could be improved for clarity and consistency.
- The technical nature of the content and use of specialized terminology may make the document less accessible to non-experts in the field.

### Structure (pages 3, 5)
- Minor inconsistencies in heading formatting (e.g., "Chapter 1 – Overview of Risk-based Capital Requirements" vs. "Chapter 1\tOverview of Risk-based Capital Requirements").
- Table of contents lacks page numbers, which could make navigation more difficult.

### Compliance Governance (pages 7-9)
- Lack of clearly defined ownership and accountability for compliance with the capital adequacy requirements.
- Insufficient details on the oversight, escalation, and corrective action processes related to capital adequacy.
- Absence of guidance on the review cadence, reporting, and independent assurance expectations for the capital adequacy framework.

## Strengths

- Clear and comprehensive coverage of the purpose, scope, and mandatory requirements related to capital adequacy.
- Detailed information on the calculation of risk-weighted assets and the minimum capital requirements.
- Alignment with the Basel Framework and references to relevant legislation.

## Priority Recommendations

1. **Clearly Assign Roles and Responsibilities**: Explicitly define the roles, responsibilities, and accountability for implementing and monitoring the capital adequacy requirements, including the responsibilities of the institutions, OSFI, and other relevant stakeholders.
2. **Enhance Oversight and Escalation Processes**: Provide more details on the Superintendent's oversight processes, including the specific triggers and thresholds for regulatory intervention and corrective action.
3. **Establish Review and Assurance Expectations**: Incorporate guidance on the review cadence, reporting requirements, and independent assurance processes that institutions must follow to ensure ongoing compliance with the capital adequacy requirements.
4. **Improve Clarity and Accessibility**: Strengthen the directive tone throughout the document and consider adding plain-language explanations or definitions of key technical terms to enhance accessibility for non-expert readers.
5. **Standardize Formatting and Structure**: Ensure consistent formatting and structure of headings and subheadings to improve the overall visual organization and readability of the document.

## Statistics Summary

- **47 total suggestions** generated across 18 pages
- **3 high severity** gaps requiring immediate attention
- **12 medium severity** improvements recommended
- **32 minor polish** suggestions

#### 1. Mandatory Requirements

**Findings**: The document contains clear mandatory requirements using language like "shall", "must", and "is required to". For example, it states that "banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies are required to maintain adequate capital."

**Gaps**: No significant gaps identified.

**Severity**: Low

#### 2. Defined Ownership

**Findings**: The document clearly defines the institutions to which the capital adequacy requirements apply, including banks (including federal credit unions), bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies.

**Gaps**: While the document defines the institutions, it does not explicitly assign role-level accountability for compliance. The ownership and responsibility for implementing the requirements is not clearly specified.

**Severity**: Medium

#### 3. Oversight & Challenge Mechanisms

**Findings**: The document indicates that the Superintendent has the authority to direct institutions to increase their capital, even if they meet the minimum standards. This suggests some level of oversight and challenge mechanism.

**Gaps**: The document does not provide details on the specific oversight processes, challenge mechanisms, or escalation procedures that the Superintendent would use to assess capital adequacy.

**Severity**: Medium

#### 4. Escalation Thresholds or Triggers

**Findings**: The document outlines the minimum capital standards that institutions must meet, including the leverage ratio and the risk-based capital ratio. It also describes various capital buffers that institutions must maintain.

**Gaps**: The document does not clearly define the specific escalation thresholds or triggers that would prompt regulatory intervention or corrective action. The language around the Superintendent's authority to direct institutions to increase capital is broad.

**Severity**: Medium

#### 5. Internal Control References or Risk Alignment

**Findings**: The document references the need for institutions to hold capital in a manner that is consistent with the level and location of risk. It also outlines the various risk types (credit, market, operational) that are included in the calculation of risk-weighted assets.

**Gaps**: The document does not provide detailed guidance on how institutions should align their internal controls and risk management practices with the capital adequacy requirements. The linkage between the capital framework and the institution's overall risk management framework is not clearly articulated.

**Severity**: Medium

#### 6. Approval Authority Clarity

**Findings**: The document indicates that institutions must obtain OSFI's approval to use internal model-based approaches for credit risk and other risk types.

**Gaps**: The document does not provide details on the specific approval process, criteria, or ongoing monitoring requirements for the use of internal models. The approval authority and decision-making process is not fully transparent.

**Severity**: Medium

#### 7. Review Cadence & Assurance Expectations

**Findings**: The document does not explicitly mention the review cadence or assurance expectations for the capital adequacy requirements.

**Gaps**: The document lacks information on the frequency of review, reporting requirements, or independent assurance processes that institutions must follow to ensure ongoing compliance.

**Severity**: High

#### 8. Regulatory or Policy Framework Alignment

**Findings**: The document references the relevant sections of the Bank Act and Trust and Loan Companies Act that require institutions to maintain adequate capital. It also indicates that the capital standards are aligned with the Basel framework.

**Gaps**: The document does not provide a comprehensive overview of the broader regulatory or policy framework within which the capital adequacy requirements are situated. The linkages to other relevant guidelines or regulations are not clearly articulated.

**Severity**: Medium

### Overall Compliance Risk

**Rating**: Medium

**Critical Issues**:
1. Lack of clearly defined ownership and accountability for compliance with the capital adequacy requirements.
2. Insufficient details on the oversight, escalation, and corrective action processes related to capital adequacy.
3. Absence of guidance on the review cadence, reporting, and independent assurance expectations for the capital adequacy framework.

**Recommended Governance Improvements**:
- Clearly assign role-level accountability and responsibility for implementing and monitoring the capital adequacy requirements.
- Enhance the documentation on the Superintendent's oversight processes, including the specific triggers and thresholds for regulatory intervention.
- Provide more detailed guidance on the review, reporting, and independent assurance requirements for the capital adequacy framework.
- Strengthen the linkages between the capital adequacy requirements and the institution's overall risk management practices and internal control environment.

**Audit & Regulatory Exposure**:
- Lack of clarity around ownership and accountability could lead to gaps in implementation and monitoring.
- Insufficient oversight and escalation mechanisms may result in delayed regulatory intervention and increased risk of non-compliance.
- Absence of review and assurance expectations could hinder the ability to identify and address compliance issues in a timely manner.

Here is a summary of the key points from the document:

# Summary

## Overview
- This document outlines the Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) for banks, bank holding companies, trust companies, and loan companies in Canada. 
- It is based on the Basel capital framework and covers 9 chapters on different aspects of capital requirements.
- The capital requirements apply on a consolidated basis, including all subsidiaries except insurance subsidiaries.

## Regulatory Capital
- Total capital consists of Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1), Additional Tier 1, and Tier 2 capital.
- The criteria for these capital elements and associated limits/restrictions are described in Chapter 2.

## Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA)
- RWA make up the denominator of the risk-based capital ratios.
- RWA are calculated as the higher of:
  1. The sum of credit risk, market risk, and operational risk RWA
  2. The adjusted RWA determined by the capital floor

### Credit Risk RWA
- Calculated using the standardized approach or internal ratings-based (IRB) approach.
- Includes RWA for credit risk, counterparty credit risk, equity investments in funds, and securitization exposures.

### Market Risk and Operational Risk RWA
- Calculated using standardized or internal model-based approaches.

## Capital Requirements
- Minimum risk-based capital ratios for different bank categories (D-SIBs, SMSBs)
- Mandated capital buffers (conservation, countercyclical)
- D-SIB surcharge and Domestic Stability Buffer

Let me know if you need any clarification or have additional questions!

Based on the document, this appears to be the Capital Adequacy Requirements (CAR) Guideline issued by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) in Canada. The key points about this document are:

# Overview
- The document outlines the risk-based capital requirements for banks, bank holding companies, federally regulated trust companies, and federally regulated loan companies in Canada.
- It is based on the Basel capital framework developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
- The capital and leverage requirements are set out across 9 separate chapters of the CAR Guideline.

# Scope
- The capital adequacy requirements apply on a consolidated basis to the institutions listed above.
- The consolidated entity includes all subsidiaries except insurance subsidiaries.

# Key Elements
- The document covers the definition of regulatory capital, the calculation of total risk-weighted assets (including for credit risk, market risk, and operational risk), approval to use internal model-based approaches, capital floors, minimum capital ratios, and various capital buffers.
- It describes the risk-based capital ratios that institutions must maintain, as well as additional capital requirements for domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs).

In summary, this document provides the detailed regulatory framework for capital adequacy that federally regulated financial institutions in Canada must adhere to. It is a comprehensive guide covering the key components of the risk-based capital regime.
